name: WindowsMenu
description:
The task was to make the `WindowsMenu` in the desktop sidebar adapt for mobile.

I explored the project and located the component at `src/components/main-menu/WindowsMenu.vue` along with its child `WindowsMenuItems.vue`.

The original popover was desktop-only: a fixed `w-[640px]` two-column panel with a `w-56` user panel and an apps grid with internal scrolling.

I proposed edits driven by the existing global `$ui.isMobile` flag: on mobile the popover becomes a `92vw` (max `420px`) stacked, single-scroll sheet (`max-h-[80vh]`), while desktop stays unchanged.

Two files were modified: `WindowsMenu.vue` (responsive width, stacked layout, `isMobile` computed) and `WindowsMenuItems.vue` (new `mobile` prop to disable nested scrolling on mobile).

messages.content: WindowsMenu in desktop side bar must be adapter for mobile

Let me get the full src structure and search specifically for "WindowsMenu".I haven't found a component literally named "WindowsMenu" yet. Let me search more broadly, including usages, stores, and the main layout files.App.vue references `DesktopSidebar.vue`, `MainMenuItems`, `WindowsMenuItems`, and `QuickBar`. Let me read the layout files and the sidebar-related components.Found it: `src/components/main-menu/WindowsMenu.vue`. Let me read it along with the related layout components.The `WindowsMenu.vue` renders a fixed 640px popover — likely not mobile-friendly. Let me read `WindowsMenuItems.vue` and `UserInfoPanel.vue`.I now have a clear picture. Let me check existing mobile patterns and the Tailwind config to follow conventions before proposing changes.I have everything I need. Here's my analysis and the proposed change. ## 1. Analysis & Pre-Thinking **Core Requirements** - The `WindowsMenu` used in the sidebar footer (`src/components/main-menu/WindowsMenu.vue`) is a Windows-style popover that is hard-coded for desktop: a **fixed 640px** two-column panel (`w-[640px]`) with a **fixed 256px left column** (`w-56`) for the user/wallet panel and a right column for the apps grid. - On mobile (viewport ≤ 1024px, where the whole sidebar becomes an overlay — `$ui.isMobile`), that layout overflows/cramps the screen and must adapt. **Strategic Approach** - Keep the same Reka-UI `Menubar`/`MenubarContent` (Portal) mechanism — no rewrite. - Drive the layout off the existing global `$ui.isMobile` flag (same flag `DesktopSidebar.vue`, `App.vue`, `ChatEntry.vue`, etc. already use). - On mobile: constrain the popover width to the viewport (`w-[92vw] max-w-[420px]`) and switch the inner body from a **side-by-side** panel to a **stacked, single-scroll sheet** (user panel on top, apps/settings below) capped at `max-h-[80vh]`. - Let `WindowsMenuItems` drop its inner `max-h-[360px] overflow-y-auto` on mobile so the sheet scrolls as one unit (avoids nested scrollbars). **Dependencies & Risks** - `$ui.isMobile` is provided by the global mixin in `main.ts` and updated on resize via `ui.handleResize` → reactive. - Desktop behavior is unchanged (the mobile classes only apply when `isMobile` is true). - `DesktopSidebar.vue` uses `WindowsMenu` in both the mobile and desktop branches; its `open`/`close` events are preserved, so no change is needed there. - Submenus (`WorkspacesMenu`, `SettingsMenu`) render in their own portals and remain functional. **Target Files** - `src/components/main-menu/WindowsMenu.vue` (modify) - `src/components/main-menu/WindowsMenuItems.vue` (modify — small) ## 2. Minimum Changes Approach 1. **WindowsMenu.vue** — add an `isMobile` computed; make the `MenubarContent` width responsive; make the inner wrapper `flex-col + overflow-y-auto` (mobile) vs `flex + w-[640px]` (desktop); make the user panel full-width top section on mobile vs `w-56` left column on desktop; pass `:mobile` to `WindowsMenuItems`. 2. **WindowsMenuItems.vue** — accept a `mobile` prop and only apply the internal `max-h-[360px] overflow-y-auto` on desktop. ## 3.
